Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:1.hebrew: שדה מגרש - מגרש הוי אלף אמה סביב לעיר, מדכתיב (במדבר ל״ה:ד׳-ה׳): "מקיר העיר וחוצה אלף אמה סביב", וחוץ לאותו אלף היה להם ללוים אלף אמה לשדות וכרמים, כדכתיב (שם): "ומדותם מחוץ לעיר וגו'" — צא מהם אלף אמה מגרש, והשאר שדות וכרמים. מגרש פנוי מכלום, ואין בו בית ואין זורעין אותן, אלא נוי הוא לעיר:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:1.english: A field [into] an empty lot - An empty lot [migrash] is a thousand cubits surrounding the city, as it is written (Numbers 35:4–5): "From the wall of the city and outward, a thousand cubits round about." And beyond that thousand [cubits], the Levites had a thousand cubits for fields and vineyards, as it is written (ibid.): "And you shall measure from outside the city, etc." [i.e., two thousand cubits] — deduct from them a thousand cubits [for] the empty lot, and the remainder [is for] fields and vineyards. An empty lot is cleared of everything: there is no house in it, and they do not sow it, rather it is an adornment for the city:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:2.hebrew: אין עושין שדה מגרש - משום יישוב ארץ ישראל, והיינו חורבן, שממעט את הזריעה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:2.english: One may not render a field an empty lot - [This is] because of the settlement of the Land of Israel, and this is [considered] destruction, as it diminishes sowing:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:3.english: Nor [may one render] an empty lot a field - because he destroys the beauty of the city:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:4.hebrew: מגרש אין עושין עיר - שיעשו בו בתים, שאין עיר נאה בלא מגרש; וכ"ש שאין עושין עיר מגרש, שאין מחריבין את יישוב העיר:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:12:4.english: One may not make an empty lot [into] a city - [meaning] that they would build houses in it, for a city is not attractive without an empty lot; and all the more so one may not make a city [into] an empty lot, for one may not destroy the settlement of the city:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:13:1.hebrew: מוכרין לעולם - אפילו בשנת היובל עצמה, כך שמעתי. וקשיא לי: אמאי? הא כי היכי דפליגי רב ושמואל בריש פירקא (לעיל ערכין כט:) בישראל שמכר שדהו בשנת היובל עצמה, ה"נ איכא לפלוגי הכא ולמימר ק"ו: מכורה כבר יוצאה עכשיו — דהא אמרינן לעיל (ערכין דף כח.) דממכרו של לוי חוזר בשנת היובל. וכמדומה לי, דאיידי דתנא באידך פירקא "מקדישין לעולם וגואלין לעולם", תנא נמי הכא:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:13:1.english: They may sell always - Even in the Jubilee year itself — so I have heard. And it is difficult for me: why? For just as Rav and Shmuel dispute at the beginning of the chapter (above, Arakhin 29b) regarding an Israelite who sold his field in the Jubilee year itself, so too there is room to dispute here and to say a kal vachomer [a fortiori] argument: [if a field that was] already sold goes out now [in the Jubilee year, then one sold now certainly does not take effect] — for we said above (Arakhin 28a) that the sale of a Levite returns in the Jubilee year. And it seems to me that since [the Tanna] taught in the other chapter, "They may consecrate always and redeem always," he also taught [this phrasing] here:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:13:2.english: [They] may redeem [them] always - for their houses in walled cities are not permanently alienated:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:16:1.hebrew: יכול אף זה - לוי כן, שאם מכר שדה אחוזתו — אותן אלף אמה שחוץ למגרש — שלא יהא מותר לגאול בפחות משתי שנים:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:16:1.english: One might [have thought that] this [one] also - [i.e.,] a Levite, [is] so, that if he sold his ancestral field — those thousand cubits that are outside the open space [around the Levitical city] — that he would not be permitted to redeem [it] in less than two years:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:17:1.hebrew: לפי שנאמר - במקדיש שדה אחוזה וגאלה אחר מיד הקדש, דבשנת היובל יוצאה לכהנים, כדכתיב "והיה השדה וגו'":
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:17:1.english: Since it is stated - [This refers to] one who consecrates an ancestral field and another [person] redeems it from the possession of the Temple treasury, [in which case] in the Jubilee year it goes out to the priests, as it is written: "But the field," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:17:2.hebrew: יכול אף - לוי כן: אם הקדיש שדה ולא גאלה, יפסידנה ביובל; ת"ל "גאולת עולם" וגו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:17:2.english: One might [have thought that] also - a Levite [is] so: if he consecrated a field and did not redeem it, he loses it at the Jubilee; [therefore] the verse states, "A perpetual right of redemption," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:1.english: These cities - [those] that are given to the Levites:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:2.hebrew: אין עושין ערים קטנים - לפי שהן ערי מקלט, ובעינן שיהא שם יישוב לבית מנוס לרוצחים:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:2.english: One does not establish [them in] small cities - because they are cities of refuge, and we require that there be a settlement there [to serve] as a place of refuge for murderers:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:3.hebrew: ולא כרכים גדולים - לפי שמתקבצין שם מכל מקומות לסחורה, ותהא רגל גואל הדם מצויה שם, ויארוב את הרוצח ויהרגנו:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:3.english: Nor large cities - because [people] gather there from all places for commerce, and [thus] the blood avenger will frequently be present there, and he will lie in wait for the killer and kill him.

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:19:4.english: Rather, intermediate towns - [which are] without a wall:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:1:1.english: Two courtyards - [This refers to] a city that has only two courtyards:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:20:1.hebrew: כאן שהוקף ולבסוף ישב - לא משכחת בהו בלוים כדקאמרת, אבל ישב ולבסוף הוקף משכחת בהו, שלאחר שניתנו להם בימי יהושע היקיפוה הם:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:20:1.english: Here, [a city] that was surrounded [by a wall] and afterwards settled - you do not find [this] among the Levites, as you said; however, [a city that was] settled [first] and afterwards surrounded [by a wall] you do find among them, for after [the cities] were given to them in the days of Joshua, they themselves surrounded it [with a wall]:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:21:1.hebrew: וכי האי גוונא - דישב ולבסוף הוקף, מי הוי חומה, דאצטריך קרא למעוטיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:21:1.english: And in a case like this - [where a city was] settled and ultimately surrounded [by a wall], is it [considered] a wall, that a verse was needed to exclude it?

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:21:2.hebrew: בית מושב עיר חומה - בית שהושב ונבנה עיר חומה, דמשמע שהוקף ולבסוף ישב:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:21:2.english: A dwelling house [in] a walled city - [This means] a house that was settled and built [in] a walled city, which implies that [the city] was [first] surrounded [by a wall] and afterward settled:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:22:1.hebrew: יכול אפילו הקיפוה ישראל - לאחר שכבשו את הארץ, ואפילו קודם שישבו בה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:22:1.english: One might [have thought] even [if] Israel surrounded it - after they conquered the Land, and even before they settled in it:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:22:2.english: And it is stated below, "a wall" - (Deuteronomy 3:5) "All these were fortified cities, etc.":

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:24:1.hebrew: תרגמה רב סלא - לעולם כשהוקף ולבסוף ישב, ודקשיא לך "עיירות הללו אין עושין אותן" כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:24:1.english: Rav Sala interpreted it - Actually, [the first baraita refers to a case] where [the city] was [first] surrounded [by a wall] and afterwards settled; and as for what is difficult for you [from the other baraita], "These cities may not be made," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:24:2.english: For example, where they fell to them - by lot, in the days of Joshua:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:2:1.hebrew: איני יודע שאין להן חומה - ד"בתי החצרים" משמע שאינו בעיר, אלא יישוב חצירות הסמוכות:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:2:1.english: Do I not know that they have no wall - For "the houses of the courtyards" implies that it is not in a [walled] city, but rather a settlement of adjacent courtyards:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:2:2.english: Like [places] that do not have a wall - Since it does not have enough [to constitute] a city:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:2:3.hebrew: וכמה - הן דלא ליחשוב חומה דידהו כעיר חומה? שתי חצרות וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:2:3.english: And how many - are they, [such] that their wall is not considered like [that of] a walled city? Two courtyards, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:3:1.hebrew: אימא בית וחצר בית וחצר - אבל אי איכא שני בתים בכל חצר, הוו כעיר חומה ולא הוו כבתי החצרים:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:3:1.english: Say [it means] a house and a courtyard, a house and a courtyard - but if there are two houses in each courtyard, they are [considered] like a walled city and are not like houses of the courtyards:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:3:2.hebrew: א"כ ליכתוב חצרים - ולא ליכתוב "בתי", ואנא ידענא דאין חצר בלא בית:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:3:2.english: If so, let [the Merciful One] write: "Courtyards" - and let [Him] not write "houses of," and I would know that there is no courtyard without a house:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:4:1.hebrew: ישראל שירש - בתי ערי חומה מאבי אמו לוי, אינו גואל כסדר הזה, שאם מכרה שתהא נחלטת ללוקח לסוף שנה, אלא לעולם גואלה כלוי, דכתיב בהו (ויקרא כ״ה:ל״ב): "גאולת עולם תהיה ללוים":
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:4:1.english: An Israelite who inherited - houses of walled cities from his mother's father, [who was] a Levite, does not redeem [them] according to this procedure — [meaning] that if he sold it, it would become permanently transferred to the buyer at the end of a year; rather, he always redeems it like a Levite, as it is written regarding them (Leviticus 25:32): "The Levites shall have an eternal right of redemption":

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:1.hebrew: עד שיהא - הוא המוכר לוי, לאפוקי ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי, דאינו גואל כלוי:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:1.english: Unless he is - [meaning] he, the seller, [is] a Levite, excluding an Israelite who inherited [a house from] his maternal grandfather [who was] a Levite, as he does not redeem [it] like a Levite:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:2.hebrew: וערי הלוים - מערים שניתנו ללוים בימי יהושע, לאפוקי בן לוי שירש את אבי אמו ישראל, דאינו גואל כלוי; והשתא קשיא רישא לסיפא, ובגמ' מתרץ לה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:2.english: And [in] the cities of the Levites - [Meaning,] from the cities that were given to the Levites in the days of Joshua, to exclude a Levite who inherited [a house from] his maternal grandfather [who was] an Israelite, [teaching] that he does not redeem [it] like a Levite; and now, the first clause [of the Mishnah] contradicts the latter clause, and in the Gemara it resolves it:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:3.hebrew: אין דברים הללו - דגאולת עולם אמורים אלא בערי הלוים, אבל "עד שיהא לוי" לא בעינן; דישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי, מודו רבנן דגואל כלוי הואיל ומערי הלוים היא זו, אבל בבן לוי שירש את אבי אמו ישראל, מודו רבנן דאינו גואל כלוי, דבערי הלוים תלא רחמנא:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:5:3.english: These matters - [i.e., the laws] of eternal redemption, are stated only [with regard to] the cities of the Levites, but we do not require "that he be a Levite"; for [in the case of] an Israelite who inherited his maternal grandfather [who was] a Levite, the Rabbis agree that he redeems like a Levite since this [house] is of the cities of the Levites, whereas in [the case of] a Levite who inherited his maternal grandfather [who was] an Israelite, the Rabbis agree that he does not redeem like a Levite, for the Merciful One made [it] dependent on "the cities of the Levites":

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:7:1.hebrew: גמ' - וקא פריך: "אינו גואל כסדר הזה" כישראל, אלא כמאן? כבן לוי — בתמיה! והא תני סיפא "עד שיהא לוי" כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:7:1.english: Gemara: And [the Gemara] asks: [If] "he does not redeem in accordance with this procedure" like an Israelite, rather, like whom [does he redeem]? Like a Levite — [said] in astonishment! But the latter clause teaches: "unless he is a Levite," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:1.hebrew: בשלמא ערי הלוים - בעינן, לאפוקי בן לוי שירש את ישראל, כדכתיב "ערי הלוים":
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:1.english: Granted, the cities of the Levites - we require [this] to exclude a Levite who inherited [a house from] an Israelite, as it is written: "the cities of the Levites":

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:2.hebrew: אלא לוי מנלן - דבעינן שיהא לוי, לאפוקי ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:2.english: But [from] where do we [derive] a Levite - that we require that he be a Levite, to exclude an Israelite who inherited [from] his mother's father, [who was] a Levite:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:3.hebrew: ואשר יגאל מן הלוים - דמשמע: למקצת לוים נתתי רשות לגאול, ולא לכולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:8:3.english: And whoever redeems from the Levites - which implies: I have given permission to some Levites to redeem, and not to all of them:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:1.hebrew: ותניא - דדרשינן הכי. ה"ג לה בתורת כהנים: "מן הלוים" מה ת"ל? שיכול לוי מישראל יגאל; כלומר, אי לא כתב אלא "גאולת עולם תהיה ללוים", יכולני לומר: לוי שמכר לישראל יגאלנה לעולם, שישראל הורע כחו בממכרו, דנחלטת לסוף שנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:1.english: And it is taught - that we expound thus. Thus we recite it in Torat Kohanim: Why does the verse state, "from the Levites"? Because [one] might [have thought that] a Levite may redeem from an Israelite — meaning, had it only written, "a perpetual right of redemption shall belong to the Levites," I could say [that] a Levite who sold [a house] to an Israelite may redeem it forever, because an Israelite's power is diminished in his [own] sale, as it becomes permanently transferred at the end of a year:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:2.hebrew: וזה יפה כחו - דכתיב "גאולת עולם" וגו', אבל לוי שמכר ללוי לא יגאל, אלא תיחלט לסוף שנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:2.english: And this [one's] power is enhanced - As it is written: "a perpetual right of redemption" etc. [Leviticus 25:32]; however, a Levite who sold [a house] to [another] Levite may not redeem [it perpetually], rather it becomes irredeemable at the end of a year:

Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:3.hebrew: ת"ל מן הלוים - פרט לבן לוי שבא מן הממזרת ומן הנתינה, וכ"ש ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי, שהרי ישראל גמור הוא:
Rashi on Arakhin 33b:9:3.english: The verse states: "From the Levites" - [This comes] to exclude the son of a Levite who was born from a mamzeret [a woman of disqualified lineage] or from a netinah [a Gibeonite descendant], and all the more so an Israelite who inherited [a house from] his maternal grandfather [who was] a Levite, since he is a full-fledged Israelite:
